actions.action: Inspect seed and roots for rot and trim any black or mushy spots before potting
Pot the seed in a deep pot (15-20 cm) with drainage and peat-free potting mix, 2-3 cm deep with shoot upward
Check soil and water when the top layer is dry
Place on a bright windowsill out of harsh direct sun and increase light gradually
If the shoot stays pale and leggy, move it to more light
After a few years, plant it outdoors

reason: The answer correctly calls the seed viable and says to plant it with gradual light, which matches the fix, but it misidentifies the lychee as a horse chestnut; nothing it recommends would hurt the seedling.
